own_initial_understanding.identity: Choice confidence is an affine transformation of the maximum predicted probability relative to 1/n. It is a statistic of predictions, not an observed correctness rate.
own_initial_understanding.mechanism_property: Subtract the uniform baseline, then divide by its distance to 1; holds for n>1 normalized nonnegative distributions. The statistic is invariant to permuting labels and depends only on n and the top probability.
own_initial_understanding.need_use: The opening asks whether a service can interpret confidence as chance of being correct. Explicit calculation and comparison with heldout outcomes prevent using 0.4 as a calibrated correctness probability.
own_initial_understanding.inputs_outputs: Given candidate probabilities and n, compute c. The caller must also preserve selected meaning and the complete distribution; a scalar cannot identify which meaning won.
own_initial_understanding.example_scope: The 0.6/0.4 example and binary/ternary comparison prove these arithmetic relations only. The 0.99-wrong and clarification examples are possibilities, not measured product behavior.
